# Twin sync: docs-links freshness + llms.txt coverage

Companion to the same change in the sibling module (its PR: "the docs build
records its inputs, and llms.txt joins the link check"). The shared invariant
is LOGIC-identical `tools/validate-docs-links.js` bodies with each repo keeping
its own narrative header - this patch preserves that: validator body is
byte-identical to the sibling's post-merge copy, header untouched.

What it adds here:

1. `tools/build-docs.js` writes `build/.build-inputs.json` (sha1 per input:
   flat `docs/*.md` + the rehype rewriter + astro config + the builder itself).
   Written to `build/`, never `build/site/` (Pages uploads that).
2. `tools/validate-docs-links.js`: a definite `STALE BUILD` block when inputs
   changed since the render (exit codes untouched; a match never claims
   freshness - Astro's content cache can replay a stale render), and an
   `llms.txt` pass resolving site-internal index links against the built tree
   (dead routes strict-fail; the site root is read off the file's own
   `Documentation:` header).
3. Eight new cases in `test/test-validate-docs-links.js`.

Apply (from this repo's root, on a fresh branch):

```bash
git apply --stat .twin-docs-links.patch     # preview
git apply .twin-docs-links.patch
npm run format:fix && npx eslint --fix tools/build-docs.js tools/validate-docs-links.js
npm run docs:build                          # writes the first manifest
npm run test:docs-links-tool
npm run quality
rm .twin-docs-links.patch .twin-docs-links-README.md
```

Then verify the twin invariant before committing:

```bash
diff <(sed -n '/^const /,$p' tools/validate-docs-links.js) \
     <(sed -n '/^const /,$p' ../bmad-module-ultracode-goal/tools/validate-docs-links.js)
```

(Expect zero output: bodies identical from the first `const` on.)

the OTHER repo's branch state by design - which is why the last two steps are
yours.

input.content:
## What this changes

The docs link validator could report a clean pass against a render that no longer matched its source, and one whole class of link — the entries in `llms.txt` — was never checked at all because that file is not HTML.

**1. The build records its inputs.** `tools/build-docs.js` now writes `build/.build-inputs.json`: one sha1 per input, covering the flat `docs/*.md` set plus the route-shaping infrastructure (both rehype rewriters, the base/site resolver, the Astro config, and the builder itself). It lands in `build/`, never `build/site/` — the site dir is what gets uploaded to Pages, and this is local bookkeeping.

The input list lives in the validator (`collectBuildInputs`) and the builder imports it, so the writer and the checker cannot drift apart about what shapes a render.

**2. The validator turns the hedge into a fact where it can.** When inputs provably changed since the render, `validate-docs-links.js` prints a definite `STALE BUILD` block naming the changed files instead of the old "results may be cached" note. A *matching* manifest deliberately keeps the hedge: Astro's content cache can replay a stale render against unchanged inputs, so a match proves nothing — only a mismatch proves staleness. Exit codes are untouched; this is diagnostic output, not a new failure mode.

**3. `llms.txt` joins the link check.** Every site-internal link in the built `llms.txt` is resolved against the built tree, with dead routes failing under `--strict`. The site root is read off the file's own `Documentation:` header rather than off the build base, so the check works regardless of what base the local render used. No file or no header means nothing is checked and a count of `0` is reported — never a pass over content that was not read.
